label: Kurvers spatial producer-scrounger evolutionary simulation
summary: Kurvers and colleagues modeled group foraging with a spatially explicit genetic algorithm whose simulated agents could alternate between producing and scrounging; the exploration level and the probability of scrounging were distinct, evolving continuous traits each ranging from 0 to 1.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

label: Foraging patch density shifts exploration and scrounging in simulation
summary: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, increasing food-patch density favored higher exploration; it also reduced scrounging at low or intermediate patch richness, but this reduction disappeared at high patch richness.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

label: Food patch richness increases modeled scrounging
summary: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, richer food patches increased evolved scrounging propensities among both fast and slow explorers, while patch richness showed no effect on evolved exploration.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

label: No stable explorer-type polymorphism within simulated environments
summary: In the Kurvers evolutionary simulations, populations within a given environmental run approached one exploration optimum rather than retaining a stable coexistence of distinct explorer personality types.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

label: Thornton meerkat provisioning and monitoring sample sizes
summary: Thornton analyzed 1,070 scorpion feeds by 347 meerkat helpers to 339 pups from 137 litters in 15 groups for prey-provisioning state, and recorded monitoring times for 6,148 feeds by 300 helpers to 244 pups from 65 litters in 13 groups.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

label: Meerkat pup age predicts intact versus disabled scorpion feeds
summary: In Thornton’s wild meerkat scorpion-feeding analysis, older pups were less likely to receive dead or disabled scorpions and more likely to receive intact scorpions, adjusting for significant modeled covariates.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

label: Helper age versus previous pup-care experience in scorpion provisioning
summary: In Thornton’s meerkat scorpion-provisioning analysis, older eligible helpers were more likely to give pups intact scorpions, whereas prior experience with earlier foraging litters showed no statistically significant association after controlling for helper age.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

label: Meerkat pup monitoring varies with prey movement size and pup age
summary: For 6,148 observed meerkat pup feeds, helpers spent longer monitoring pups when provisioned prey was moving or larger and spent less time monitoring as pups grew older.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

label: Meerkat monitoring duration declines with nearby helpers and rain
summary: In Thornton’s meerkat feeding observations, pup monitoring duration decreased with larger litter size, higher recent rainfall, and the presence of another helper within two metres.
